correctness.rationale: The published PGF factors exactly as p0(1+b*s)(1-r*s)/(1-q*s)^2; hence all formal log coefficients are (2q^k-r^k+(-1)^(k+1)b^k)/k. The discrete ID iff positive CP intensities criterion follows from n-th PGF roots and converse exponential construction. For b<=q all coefficients are positive and summable, whereas for b>q every sufficiently large even coefficient is negative. The k*log(b/q)->log2 first-obstruction law follows from bounding e^(kt)+(r/q)^k for small t uniformly over finite and large k. Actual standalone standard-library checker passed 1384 finite/formula assertions. No finite check is used for the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The BPL model is an established count regression family. Its compound-Poisson representation is exactly the cluster-process interpretation relevant to aggregation and accident frequencies. This is a complete sharp parameter classification, not a chosen low-degree necessary condition; moreover it proves an exact near-boundary divergence of the first detecting coefficient and an overdispersed non-ID example, warning that finite diagnostics can misclassify the model. The result has mathematically motivated structural content beyond a routine moment calculation.
